page_title: Lurar — system-wide audio EQ for macOS

summary.name: Lurar
summary.one_liner: Lurar is a free, open source macOS app that applies system-wide headphone correction, using a 10-band parametric EQ and the built-in AutoEq preset catalog.
use_cases: correct headphone frequency response on a Mac
apply AutoEq presets to headphones or IEMs system-wide
compare EQ curves with blind A/B listening tests
use crossfeed for more natural headphone imaging
EQ audio from Spotify, browsers and other apps without installing a driver
auto-switch EQ presets when changing output devices
summary.what_it_does: Lurar captures each app's audio using Apple's Core Audio Process Tap API, runs it through a 10-band parametric EQ tuned to chosen headphones from the AutoEq catalog, and sends the result to the selected output device. It lets users browse and search the AutoEq library, fork presets, and edit bands with a live spectrum analyzer and clip meter. It includes blind and sighted A/B comparison with loudness matching, Bauer-style crossfeed, and ISO 226:2003 loudness compensation. It remembers the preset per output device and can sync its preset library through iCloud.
notable: Uses Apple's Process Tap API, so no virtual audio driver or kernel extension is needed
Blind A/B mode with broadband RMS loudness matching
Per-device preset memory and iCloud preset sync
Open source (MIT), no account, no telemetry
caveats: Apps using HAL exclusive mode cannot be tapped and so cannot be EQ'd
Conflicts with Rogue Amoeba ARK driver tools such as SoundSource, Audio Hijack and Loopback
